design.affected_system: public participation, multilingual communication, consultation, and feedback closure
alternatives: verify the highest-consequence signals before acting on public participation and feedback-process gaps
combine targeted inspection, monitoring, and data-quality repair for public participation and feedback-process gaps
pair stage-specific denominator and contribution pathway diagnosis with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Invitation, exposure, participation, contribution, response, decision, and trust remain distinct.
Participation records preserve consent, privacy, language, accessibility, and channel provenance.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue current inspection and reporting practice for public participation and feedback-process gaps.

constraints.description: The public participation and risk communication diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: public engagement director and risk communications lead
design.decision_question: Which affected groups and issues are missing across invitation, access, participation, response, and closure stages?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The public participation and risk communication diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for public participation and feedback-process gaps passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: stage-specific denominator and contribution pathway diagnosis
independence_key.primary_outcome: affected people without usable participation and feedback access

design.intended_claim: A versioned diagnose design for comparing declared alternatives affecting public participation and feedback-process gaps, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: affected people without usable participation and feedback access
distributional gap in affected people without usable participation and feedback access
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not label nonparticipation apathy, opposition, consent, satisfaction, or lack of concern.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for public participation and feedback-process gaps passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

design.title: Diagnose participation, representation, and feedback gaps
transportability_risks: Trust, language, civic institutions, digital access, deliberation norms, and risk salience differ.
Participants are not automatically representative of affected populations.

family.affected_system: public participation, multilingual communication, consultation, and feedback closure
claim_boundary: Area and administrative differences do not establish discrimination, preferences, or individual behavior.
Behavioral and allocation designs require rights, accessibility, privacy, and non-coercion review.
Causal, fairness, adoption, and welfare claims require direct outcomes and independent governance evidence.
family.decision_owner: public engagement director and risk communications lead
family.description: Eight decisions for participation-gap diagnosis, engagement forecasting, inclusion portfolios, venue siting, outreach allocation, communication schedules, misinformation stress, and evaluation.
family.title: Public participation and risk communication

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
